$comment: The KernelSU late-load build for this target. A run of it reached a loaded,
answering KernelSU on the device: module Live, /data/adb/ksud installed,
`su` returning uid 0 in u:r:ksu:s0, and SELinux back to Enforcing.
ddkImage below is NOT what produced that module, and this file cannot yet
say what did. The generic android12-5.10 DDK is only an approximation of
this kernel -- Meta builds its own rather than shipping GKI -- and a module
built from it rebooted the device on load every time, three runs out of
three, while resolving every symbol. CFI, LTO, SCS and PAC all match; what
does not is 104 options that are =y on the device and absent from the DDK,
four of them guarding task_struct fields (KASAN, PREEMPT_NOTIFIERS,
TASK_DELAY_ACCT, and UBSAN_TRAP compiling traps into the module).
What produced the module that works: Meta's own source for this build,
kernel/oculus-linux-kernel, branch oculus-quest3-kernel-master,
HEAD 'Oculus Quest 3 kernel project build: 5234532.3540.520'
= ro.build.version.incremental 52345320035400520
with the device's own /proc/config.gz as .config, built with the DDK
image's toolchain (its Android clang r416183b builds 5.10; the host's
clang-21 does not) and used as KDIR for an external module build. A full
kernel build is not needed and does not finish here -- Qualcomm's vendor
drivers fail on tracepoint includes -- but modules_prepare alone is not
enough either: KernelSU's selinux part needs the generated
security/selinux/flask.h, which the failed full build produces before it
stops.
So the action would need a way to take a kernel tree instead of a DDK
image before it could build this target. Until it does, ddkImage names the
closest KMI so the entry is well-formed and says which one it is; building
from it produces a module that reboots the device on load.
Measured on the device and worth keeping:
- CONFIG_MODULES=y and CONFIG_MODULE_SIG unset, so unsigned modules load.
- CONFIG_MODVERSIONS=y, answered as everywhere else here by an empty
Module.symvers and a zero-length __versions section, with ksud
resolving the 48 unexported symbols from /proc/kallsyms.
- kptr_restrict is 2, which hides every kallsyms address from root as
well; the bootstrap helper now sets 0 across the load and restores it.
- The audit decides the KMI, not the ship date:
extract_target_symvers.py against a vmlinux recovered from the running
kernel, then audit_module_against_target.py. MISSING_SYMBOL is fatal,
MISSING_EXPORT is not. android14-6.1 gives 10, android12-5.10 gives 1,
the real source gives 0.
devices/quest3 is upstream 953b403a backported onto the pinned 32525. It
keeps the tracepoint mark on /system/bin/stub_zygote, which is how Horizon
OS starts the zygote; without it a `ksud soft-reboot` brings back a zygote
no KernelSU hook fires for, and the manager dies with SIGSYS on its first
supercall. The set exists at 32514 and 32525 and deliberately not at
32567, which already carries the commit: a pin move to it fails this build
until the name is taken out of patchSets, which is the reminder wanted.
